Curlimp brings browser profiles to your terminal through a Rust CLI and a bundled, modified libcurl engine.

## Try it with Docker

```sh
docker run --rm juanfontes/curlimp:0.3.0 -sS -I https://httpbin.org/status/200
docker run --rm juanfontes/curlimp:0.3.0 firefox147 --json-output -sS -i https://httpbin.org/status/418
```

The image supports Linux amd64 and arm64. Chrome 150 is the default profile, and responses are decompressed automatically. Use an exact profile before the URL or `--impersonate PROFILE` to select another browser.

## Native downloads

Choose `linux-amd64`, `linux-arm64`, or the experimental `macos-arm64` archive. Download `SHA256SUMS`, verify the matching archive, extract it and keep the entire bundle together. Run `./curlimp --version` from its directory. The native packages include their engine, dependency notices and Zsh profile-completion script.

On Linux, verify with `sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing`. On macOS, select your archive's line from `SHA256SUMS` and pass it to `shasum -a 256 --check`. See the [installation guide](https://juanfontes.github.io/curlimp/docs/installation/) for complete commands and PATH setup.

The macOS package is signed ad hoc and is not notarized. Its deployment target is macOS 13.0; CI validates macOS 15. Windows and Intel Mac native packages are not available.

## Features

- 39 browser and HTTP-client profiles, listed with `curlimp --list-profiles`.
- Familiar curl-style options for requests, redirects, authentication, headers, cookies, proxies and response output.
- `--txt` and `--json-file` save timestamped response files. `--json-output` prints structured JSON. Body-only, `-i` headers/body and `-I` headers-only selection are preserved; curl's `--json DATA` still sends request JSON.
- Zsh profile completion with prefix matching of any length. Add `source <(curlimp --completions zsh)` after `compinit` in `~/.zshrc`; see the [autocomplete guide](https://juanfontes.github.io/curlimp/docs/completion/).

## Validation and limits

Each platform builds its native engine from verified source inputs and tests the extracted bundle. Checks cover HTTP/TLS/HTTP2 behavior, profiles, response exports, certificate overrides and Zsh completion. Linux also tests the minimal runtime filesystem.

Curlimp supports one HTTP(S) URL per invocation and a documented subset of curl flags. It does not open a browser or execute JavaScript. HTTP/3 behavior and fingerprint equivalence to real browsers remain unverified. JSON exports buffer at most 64 MiB; TXT exports stream bytes. Docker file exports need a host volume mount.
